subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu text commands (/stop, /new, /status) no longer bypass queue during active agent run (3.8 regression)

question: Should Feishu whole-message text commands during active runs fast-path only safe local commands, or should stateful commands such as `/stop` and `/new` also become authorized queue-bypassing text command turns?
rationale: Current main and the latest release split command classes differently; deciding which stateful commands may bypass Feishu queue/session ordering is a product and safety decision, not a mechanical cleanup.

options.title: Choose policy before another fix
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers select the command boundary, then implement the selected Feishu command-turn and queue behavior in one focused PR.

options.title: Narrow to safe local commands
options.body: Only fast-path read-only/local operational replies such as `/status`, and track `/stop` and `/new` separately until maintainers accept the broader stateful behavior.

options.title: Restore all reported commands
options.body: Treat `/status`, `/stop`, and `/new` as authorized Feishu text-command turns that bypass active-run blocking, with tests and live proof for stateful behavior.

recommendation.title: Choose policy before another fix
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers select the command boundary, then implement the selected Feishu command-turn and queue behavior in one focused PR.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice crosses command authorization, command-turn semantics, and queue/session behavior where steipete has the strongest feature-history signal.
